item.title: Rooftop Pollinator Garden Maintenance (Raleigh) — Fri Aug 21, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Now that the school year is almost upon us, NCWF South Wake Conservationists Chapter is returning the rooftop garden at Southeast Raleigh Elementary School to keep it in shape! It’s time to follow up our earlier summer weedings, and prepare them for the students’ reurn later this month. The sixteen tall beds fully dedicated to pollinators are in need of some weeding. Between the drought and the resiliance of invasive grasses and other plants, the pollinator plants have had a rough summer. This is where we need your assistance! Can you help? This rooftop garden is a very popular and meaningful program to the students and administration. Just bring your personal water bottle and a pair of gardening gloves, and we’ll supply the rest. Hope you can join us! REGISTER HERE
Source: NC Wildlife Federation

item.title: THE LONG EXHALE | A GROUP EXHIBITION - Third Friday Opening Reception — Fri Aug 21, 6:00 PM — 5 Points Gallery
item.description:
5 Points Gallery is pleased to present The Long Exhale, bringing together work by the ten artists of 5 Points Gallery. As the pace of summer begins to soften, The Long Exhale invites visitors to pause, look closely, and linger. The exhibition offers a refreshing mix of painting, sculpture, fused glass, mixed media, and finely crafted furniture, with each artist offering a distinct creative perspective. Join us for the Opening Reception on Friday, August 21, 2026, from 6–9 pm to meet the artists. The exhibition runs from August 20 through September 12, 2026. Visit 5 Points Gallery in person or online at https://5pointsgallery.com. All work from the exhibition is available for shipping or pickup. Gallery hours: Thursdays and Fridays 5–9pm and Saturdays 1–9pm. Artists are available to talk about their work. For a private viewing, contact us at info@5pointsgallery.com.

item.title: Third Friday at DAC-opening of two new shows! — Fri Aug 21, 6:00 PM — Durham Arts Council
item.description:
Join us at the Durham Arts Council for Third Friday! We are celebrating the opening of two new shows in our galleries. In the Allenton gallery, Christa Capua’s “The Hours After Helene” is an ode to the Book of Hours, and finding strength after natural disasters, all through Capua’s unique southern futurism photocollage works. Upstairs in the Semans gallery, two artists share “Rooted in Joy”, which celebrates the botanical works of Kristin Gibson and Charisse Coleman. Gibson’s unique still life paintings which use the alla-prima painting method, and Coleman’s original eco-prints, highlight a love of nature, and urge the viewers to take a breath and enjoy. There will be light fare, drinks, and free activities.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.description:

Make sure that your bike is in good working order - tires hold air and are up to pressure, brakes and shifters work and your chain has been oiled.

item.title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star (Theatre for the Very Young) — Thu Aug 27, 10:00 AM — Raleigh Little Theatre
item.description:
Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star is an interactive children’s theatre piece for very young audiences, performed by two Star Keepers named Glimmer and Sparkle. It’s time for the night sky to fill with stars, but one important star — Little Star, the wishing star — is missing because Sparkle rushed through putting the stars away the previous morning and muddled everything up. What follows is a search-and-rescue adventure as the two star keepers (and the audience) hunt for Little Star, discovering along the way that all the other stars have been put in the wrong places too and need to be moved to their proper place. Audience members help the Star Keepers find and re-organize the sky just in time for nightfall so that everyone can make a wish on their favorite star. Twinkle, Twinkle explores the ideas that mistakes happen, feelings are valid, and no one has to face hard things alone – all wrapped up in a genuinely joyful romp about stars.
By Ernie Nolan Produced by special arrangemen

item.title: Get Shit Done - SQSN — Tue Sep 1, 5:30 PM — 114 - living room
item.description:
This event is intended for Queer and/or Trans survivors: Some of the biggest barriers to survivor safety are finance related. While we do our best to put cash directly into survivors hands, in tandem, we thought it would be awesome to create a body doubling/coworking space where we can support each other in sifting through all the shit that goes into getting financial stable. And offer relevant financial resources as we find them! That’s why we host our “Get Shit Done” evenings. They will occur the 1st & 3rd Tuesday of each month and be available in person or online (must register or email advocate@lgbtqcenterofdurham.org for the virtual link). Find the registration link in our bio :) If you or someone you know is a money expert who wants to share their knowledge with queer/trans survivors, please reach out!
Source: LGBTQ Center of Durham

item.title: Luminary & Freedom Stories — Fri Sep 18, 7:00 PM — Bennett Place State Historic Site
item.description:
During this special luminary program, Bennett Place invites you to reflect on the end of the Civil War as a momentous step towards freedom for all Americans and the end of chattel slavery in the United States.
Walk among 3,310 luminaries - one for every 1,000 enslaved people in North Carolina - and reflect on experiences of enslavement and freedom. Historians dot the path and share stories of people's pathways to freedom and life after slavery & the Civil War.
---
Harriet Ann Daves recalled just how monumental Civil War surrenders were for her family: "When the surrender came my grandfather came to my mother and told her: 'Well, you are as free as I am.'"
Claiming freedom was not so straightforward for the 331,059 enslaved women, children, and men in North Carolina during the Civil War. item.title: Meet Your Plant Neighbors — Sat Sep 26, 6:30 PM — Old Creedmoor Nature Preserve
item.description:
Join TLC for an exploration of plants at Old Creedmoor Nature Preserve! Which plants do we live amongst? What are their names? What are their stories? On this 1.4-mile hike, we will celebrate Public Lands Day by meeting our plant neighbors at TLC's newest preserve, Old Creedmoor. We'll amble along Lizard's Tail Loop identifying trees, shrubs, and herbs along the way. All levels of plant knowledge are welcome -- we are a community of learners and sharers!
This is a free event, but preregistration is required. The group will return to the parking lot by sunset, but please bring a flashlight or headlamp just in case visibility begins to lower at the end of the hike.
If registration is full, please fill out the waitlist form here by September 24th at noon.
Source: Triangle Land Conservancy
